AUDIT r11 M11-4. The census's guards were pinned by mutation rows, and its verdict COMPOSITION was pinned by nothing: dropping `and bodyful(fid)[0]` from the criteria dict left `--selftest` at 34/34, check_census_arms at all_mutated_or_accounted, and every gate green -- only R7 FRESH fired, and its own printed remedy re-pins the mutated file after replaying the MUTANT's own selftest, which passes. Counting the shapes of refusals cannot catch that. This pins the OUTPUT: the census is run on a committed synthetic dump and its verdict surface must match, so any change that moves a result on these five functions fails, whatever form the change takes.
The fixture is built to exercise each path that decides a verdict: a body whose closure is clean (clean::good -> clean::helper), a body that escapes into a declaration and is lifted by the discharge table (clean::escapes -> clean::declared_only), a body with a call_indirect that must fail closed (clean::indirectly), and the body/declaration partition itself.

AUDIT r12 M12-2 widened this fixture. It had four bodies with lowered / spliced / zero_unsupported / derived_agreed / flip_event_O3 all CONSTANT-TRUE, so mutating any of those five criteria to `True` was MISSED -- only bodyful_reachable_closure (the one r11's exploit happened to use) was watched. Measured impact of that gap on real data: `"flip_event_O3": True` mints a0_complete_6_of_6 189 -> 1149 in data/crystal_a0_census_2026-08-27.json, the figure CLAUDE.md quotes for the A0 owner ruling, with every gate green. Each criterion is now FALSE on exactly one body so every cell discriminates; the discharge target carries TWO escaping callees, because the real target (level::Level::is_zero) has two and `escapes[:1]` was likewise a missed mutation. A sixth body, clean::partial, escapes to BOTH declarations while the table covers only the first: the full loop refuses it and `escapes[:1]` would wrongly lift it, so the escape-set CARDINALITY discriminates too.

AUDIT r13 M13-7: five PINNED cells still had no discrimination after r12 -- the flip logs contained zero `CTFE compiled from trust` lines (real logs carry 41) so the CTFE/codegen split never ran; flips_O3 and flips_O0 were byte-identical so the argument ORDER was unpinned; and every coverage row carried markers_detail null with no markers_exact and no lineage, so markers_vacuous, markers_exact and a6_event_lineage_equal were constant-FALSE. Measured on real dumps: deleting the CTFE branch mints a0_complete_6_of_6 189 -> 230, forcing markers_vacuous False takes the published non-vacuous figure 36 -> 189, and swapping O0/O3 gives 189 -> 205 -- all with the pin green. The fixture now exercises the CTFE branch, gives O0 a different content from O3, and varies markers and lineage across bodies. The ADEQUACY ASSERTION below is what keeps it that way: every pinned per-body boolean must take BOTH values across the fixture, so the pin cannot silently lose discrimination again.
